evidenceSections.sourceIdentity: W3C PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
evidenceSections.locator: Bundle definition — a named set of provenance descriptions that is itself an entity.
evidenceSections.supports: That a set of provenance descriptions can be named and treated as an entity in its own right, so that the provenance of provenance can be expressed and a reader can ask who asserted a given account.

limitations: A model for expressing provenance, not a guarantee of it. Naming a bundle does not make its contents accurate, and the specification does not establish that any recorded graph is complete.

evidenceSections.sourceIdentity: JCGM 200:2012, International Vocabulary of Metrology (VIM), 3rd edition
evidenceSections.supports: That measurement error is the measured quantity value minus a reference quantity value, and therefore presupposes a reference against which the measurement is compared.

limitations: Error in the metrological sense, requiring a reference value. It is not model error, prediction error, or a mistake in a procedure, and it does not define uncertainty, which the same vocabulary treats as a separate concept.

specifications.directAnswer: Traceability — Tradeoffs: Understand Traceability through the tradeoffs lens in Policy Clearing on policy.mahastrategies.com.
specifications.context: This route applies urn:maha:concept:governance:traceability under the owner-application contract. The canonical definition remains with maha-policy.

evidenceSections.sourceIdentity: JCGM 200:2012, International Vocabulary of Metrology (VIM), 3rd edition
evidenceSections.locator: §2.41 (6.10), definition of metrological traceability, with Note 1.
evidenceSections.supports: That metrological traceability is a property of a measurement result: the result can be related to a reference through a documented unbroken chain of calibrations, each contributing to the measurement uncertainty.

limitations: This is traceability of a measurement to a reference standard. It is not provenance of a document, lineage of a citation, or an audit trail of a system, all of which share the word. A page about record traceability must not cite this definition.

evidenceSections.sourceIdentity: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3, Incident Response Recommendations and Considerations for Cybersecurity Risk Management
evidenceSections.locator: Executive Summary, paragraph placing incident response across the six CSF 2.0 Functions.
evidenceSections.supports: That incident response is treated as part of cybersecurity risk management rather than a standalone activity, and is distributed across the Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover functions.

limitations: Recommendations and considerations, not a reporting obligation. It sets no disclosure deadline, names no regulator, and does not establish when an incident must be reported to anyone.
